title: Prompt Sentinel Matrix, Regression Severity Tiers, and Staged Rollback Choreography for Optimize v2
creator: Alicia Mendez
description:
Purpose: Define a production-ready quality gating and rollback choreography for Optimize model rollouts. This ticket captures the PRD-level requirements for prompt sentinel composition, multi-tier regression severity rules, A/B criteria for canaries, and the automated/manual actions that should occur when signals cross thresholds. The goal is to make rollouts safe and actionable while minimizing unnecessary rollbacks and customer noise.

Background: Recent experiments with quantized model variants and batching changes produced subtle downstream quality regressions in targeted cohorts. Current guardrails are ad-hoc (manual dashboards and pager alerts) and do not codify graduated responses. This PRD standardizes signal definitions and explicit remediation steps so Product, SRE, and Runtime can automate first-line mitigations and surface only actionable incidents to on-call.

Scope:
- Design prompt sentinel sampling matrix (core sentinels, exploratory, adversarial probes) and provenance labels.
- Define composite quality score and per-cohort metrics (accuracy proxy, hallucination rate, instruction-following, toxicity score).
- Specify multi-tier regression thresholds (warning/critical/blocking) with statistical tests and minimum sample sizes.
- Define A/B canary rules: when to stop, pause, or rollback.
- Orchestrate staged rollback choreography (automated rollback, traffic-shaping, model variant fallback).

Out of scope:
- New instrumentation implementations (this ticket defines requirements; separate eng tickets will implement metrics export).
- UI/console design for dashboards (tracked in a separate design ticket).
acceptance_criteria: A1: A sentinel matrix is defined with at least three tiers: core (2k prompts), exploratory (10k prompts), adversarial (1k prompts) and each prompt labeled with cohort provenance (app-type, token-length-band, instruction-complexity).

A2: Composite quality score formula published: weighted combination of exact-match/intent-score (40%), hallucination proxy (30%), instruction-following (20%), toxicity delta (10%) and baseline snapshot stored for each model variant.

A3: Regression tiers defined with numerical thresholds and tests: WARNING = change >= 1.5% relative drop with p < 0.05 on N>=1000; CRITICAL = change >= 3.0% with p < 0.01 on N>=2000; BLOCKING = change >= 5.0% regardless of p (manual review immediate).

A4: A/B canary rules codified: minimum sample size 5k requests per variant, sequential analysis with alpha-spending (overall alpha 0.05), minimum detectable effect 1.5% for core cohort, stop-and-hold action when CRITICAL triggers in core cohort for two sequential windows (1 hour windows).
A5: Latency/error SLOs integrated into gating: P99 token latency increase >20% or 5xx rate >0.5% in canary triggers automatic traffic cutoff for that variant and routes to previous stable variant.

A6: Rollback choreography documented with exact remediation actions: automatic rollback (immediate for BLOCKING), staged rollback (25% -> 0% over 30m if CRITICAL), and soft-mitigation (reduce concurrency/disable quantization) for WARNING. Documentation includes runbook links.
A7: Monitoring hooks and dashboard links are enumerated (prometheus metrics, composite-signal evaluator, and canary dashboard). Placeholder dashboards defined so engineering can implement alerts.
decision_log: D1: Use composite weighted score instead of single metric to reduce noisy rollbacks; weights chosen by PM + Research after a small sensitivity study (weights above).
D2: Implement both statistical test and absolute blocking thresholds to catch rare catastrophic regressions that tests might miss given small sample sizes.
D3: Canary minimum sample sizes chosen to balance time-to-detect with per-traffic cost; we prefer sequential analysis to avoid fixed-window false positives.
open_questions: Q1: Should toxicity delta be capped per cohort to avoid noisy signals from low-volume safety-critical customers?
Q2: What is the authoritative baseline snapshot cadence (daily vs. per-release)? Proposal: snapshot at release + daily rolling baseline for drift detection.

Q3: Do we allow automated rollback for quantization-only changes, or require human-in-loop for all model-architecture-altering rollouts? Recommended: quantization auto-mitigate, weight/architecture changes require approval.

WI-2: Define composite score implementation spec and export schema (owner: Runtime Metrics)

WI-4: Add automated rollback API integration to orchestration layer (owner: Serving Runtime)

rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal validation against core sentinels (dev-only) - block for any BLOCKING-level regressions.
Phase 1: Closed beta to 1% traffic (24h baseline) - auto-stop if CRITICAL triggers in core cohort for two sequential 1h windows.
Phase 2: Ramp to 25% over 48 hours with continuous sequential testing and hourly summary reports - soft-mitigations applied on WARNING signals.
Phase 3: Ramp to 100% over 7 days conditional on no CRITICAL or BLOCKING signals and stabilization of composite score within +/-0.75% of baseline.
rollback_choreography: BLOCKING: immediate automated rollback to previous stable variant; create incident ticket and notify on-call PM + SRE; preserve canary logs for postmortem.

CRITICAL: immediate traffic cut for canary variant; route traffic to stable variant; start 30-minute staged rollback (25%->0%) if automated rollback fails; require on-call human review within 60 minutes.
WARNING: apply soft-mitigation (disable quantization, reduce concurrency, or reduce batching), continue monitoring for 3 windows; escalate to CRITICAL if signals persist or worsen.
metrics_and_alerts: Composite quality delta (weighted) vs baseline; alert on WARNING/CRITICAL/BLOCKING thresholds per cohort.
P99 token latency delta; alert at >20% increase in canary cohort.
Error (5xx) rate; alert at >0.5% absolute increase in canary cohort.
User-visible degradation signals (billing anomalies, replay test failures) integrated into composite score.
risks: R1: Overly sensitive thresholds could cause unnecessary rollbacks and harm user trust; mitigation: initial conservative thresholds + staged tuning window.
R2: Insufficient sentinel coverage may miss regressions in niche cohorts; mitigation: iterative expansion and stratified sampling plan.
R3: Automation bugs in rollback API could produce flapping; mitigation: implement safety locks and require two independent signals for automated rollback for non-BLOCKING cases.
